plan.title: Confounded lung treated vs control DE + pathway analysis
plan.analytical_narrative: 12 lung RNA-seq samples (6 treated, 6 control; salmon-derived raw gene counts, 12000 genes) are compared for treated-vs-control differential expression. The batch variable is perfectly confounded with condition (all controls = B1, all treated = B2), so a batch term cannot be fit and no batch-correction/SVA method can be applied without removing the condition effect itself — the design's rank does not allow separating the two. The plan therefore proceeds with a single-factor DESeq2 model (~condition) exactly as grounded by the knowledge service, but every downstream result is explicitly labeled as confounded: any treated-vs-control effect detected is statistically indistinguishable from a batch/processing effect, and the report must state this in place of a mechanistic claim. QC first characterizes whether the primary variance axis is condition/batch (they are inseparable here) and flags sample-level outliers. DE runs via DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm shrinkage and BH-adjusted independent filtering at alpha=0.05. Enrichment runs fgsea preranked on the Wald statistic against MSigDB Hallmark (staged, human, 2026.1) and Reactome (staged, current) as a follow-up collection. The final report synthesizes DE and enrichment results with the confounding caveat stated up front, full reproducibility metadata, and fit diagnostics.
